_note: Bounds fixed before the notebook is run. Every gate in Session 5 is one of two kinds and there are no others. (1) REPRODUCTION: a digit some frozen artefact already carries -- the corpus manifest, Session 2's published baselines, chapter 14's printed figures, the recorded run in recorded_*.json -- which this notebook has to return. A reproduction bound has no preferred direction: it would pass exactly as it does now if the embedding signal in block B had validated, if the byte-identical repeat in block D had agreed more than the reworded prompt, and if text had improved the forecast in block F, because what it compares against is a recorded number and not a threshold. (2) PROCEDURE: a property of how the run was done -- hashes checked before a byte is read, every fitted object confined to the 1994-2014 window, the attention map causal, the test window scored once and a second attempt refused. No gate anywhere in this notebook is on an outcome. Nothing passes because a number came out large, or small, or in a direction the lab would prefer.
_no_pilot: Session 4 took the bounds of its torch blocks from a five-seed pilot because those blocks were graded on a loss. Session 5 grades no block on a loss: the torch work in block C is a forward pass in eval mode, a seeded sample, and sixty seeded training steps, and what is gated about it is structural -- the parameter count, the file hashes, the causal mask, the held-out split. So there is no pilot file beside this one, and no bound below was chosen by watching a distribution of seeds.
